findings_and_questions.status: Historical 774 open availability condition independently refined at 95e; no new unique count or observed failure
findings_and_questions.observation: Roster helper replaces membership query failure with an empty list and removes missing/failed character rows and observer-ineligible members. The selected quest party_readiness initializes true and visits only retained alive views, so an empty or completely filtered list returns true; when other control and case conditions pass, that value reaches can_fight and the case-site page model. Independently the native require_party_ready builds living IDs from authoritative rows and rejects an empty authoritative living list.
findings_and_questions.qualification: This is static control-flow reasoning only. No query failure, eligible site, party, rendered control, click or invalid action was observed. A missing/filtered UI roster can be distinct from a genuinely empty authoritative roster; no claim every action uses that native gate or that native authorization is bypassed. Exact q1869/774/availability alias and whether user-facing readiness must be unknown remain central. The helper does not establish a fresh current checkpoint or product validation.
findings_and_questions.future_repair_direction: After completing audit and with later implementation authorization, preserve roster/readiness completeness as a distinct observation and bind UI decisions to the intended authoritative roster while maintaining observer-time privacy and backend authority.

nonfindings: Observer-frontier helper deliberately fails closed when subject time is ahead or chronology cannot be established. project_alive_as_observed deliberately treats broad current dead as alive when observer/death chronology is unavailable or future, to avoid revealing death outside observer time; it is a transient view, not a server resurrection or authority grant.

The current project_alive_as_observed body handles observed chronology query errors internally and returns Ok on those paths; the roster outer Err branch is an additional defensive fallback, not proof of a presently reachable Err from that specific body.

Native require_party_ready rejects no living members. The selected quest helper fails closed on refresh or individual condition query failure for each included member, but an empty input skips that loop; the two facts must not be collapsed.
A no-party roster returning empty and genuinely unarmed or empty inventories can be legitimate; no blanket empty-is-invalid rule follows.

The inventory meter shows a derived summary and does not by itself prove combat receives extra encumbrance, fatigue or movement penalties. User combat rule requires one fatigue pool, encumbrance once through incapacitation, projected yellow only, and no pre-incapacitation movement penalty.
Source tests were read only. No product, fixture, test, build, browser, runtime probe or simulation was run.

Which native action reducers call require_party_ready, and how do they handle same-date identity, current life and omitted observation differently from the UI?
What observer-time and snapshot policy applies to equipment appearance, visible membership, co-location and social state, especially asynchronous frontiers?
Which independently valid empty inventories, catalogs, food/liquid/condition rows are allowed, and which absence or query failure must produce explicit unknown rather than a numeric burden?
Does actual downstream profile infer leader from visible list order, and are q201/roster availability causes unique or shared?
All strategic/tactical wheel producers, consumers, colors and remaining path-specific sources require separate review; exact cross-lens aliases and repair ordering remain central.

thirteen_lenses.producer-propagation: Membership -> observed character views -> selected quest readiness and inventory burden; native actual living IDs/authority remain separate. Independent queries and lost completeness are documented conditions, not confirmed runtime states.
thirteen_lenses.existing-type-owners: CharacterView, StrategicMinute, EncumbranceSummary and native member IDs serve distinct domains. Typed leaf presence does not by itself certify a complete roster or snapshot.
thirteen_lenses.admission-contracts: Native readiness checks actual living members and rejects empty; web observer filter and failed queries carry different admission/availability semantics. The root fatigue/encumbrance contract remains authoritative.
thirteen_lenses.invariant-operations: EncumbranceSummary normalizes scalar values and combines load/capacity, but cannot restore missing input provenance. Empty all-fold returns true in selected web readiness, contingent on its input.
thirteen_lenses.aggregate-states: A roster, time frontier, life projection, leader, member inventory and aggregate burden require correlated completeness; presence or typed rows independently do not guarantee it.
thirteen_lenses.type-ownership: Strategic database owns action and living-party authority; web owns observer-time projections and display. Social and equipment appearance have separate privacy/visibility contracts needing exact owner trace.
thirteen_lenses.redundant-authority: Web readiness is a presentation estimate and native readiness is an authority gate; they have different roles, but silently reusing incomplete projection as a complete estimate is the conditional issue.
thirteen_lenses.behavior-preservation: Preserve fail-closed future visibility and intentional concealment of unknown/future deaths, valid no-party state, legitimate unarmed/empty input and separate native authorization. No compatibility fallback should be added.
thirteen_lenses.enum-shapes: Held equipment channel and appearance anchors are typed; absence, error, future-hidden and observed-alive are distinct semantic states whose current collapsing remains a policy question.
thirteen_lenses.derivability: Derived/default summary construction and vector accumulation alone do not guarantee complete source data; no blanket derive or serialization replacement is justified.
thirteen_lenses.granularity: Separate observer-visible roster from authoritative live roster, leader identity from order, per-member burden from pooled custody, and preview from gameplay impairment.
thirteen_lenses.magic-strings: Escaped party SQL strings and logging are native interface boundaries; retained source IDs require further actual graph owner proof. No automatic private prose classifier finding.
thirteen_lenses.magic-numbers: Concurrency 4 bounds concurrent member tasks, not a global backend limit; leg strength conversion constants belong to existing physical owner. Do not infer an extra fatigue pool or pre-incapacitation speed penalty.

limitations: Static source and offline evidence-integrity inspection only. No source/publication edits, repairs, builds, tests, fixture or product execution, browser, probes or simulations. Historical authors, scope and snapshot identities remain distinct; central owns alias reconciliation, repair ledger and publication.
